event: Nala says, "I'm afraid I am new to the lands. You would know better than I."
"Based on the targeting nature of the damage, only affecting Zhao Jun,"
"I would have expected humans as the source."
"Were it not for the tracks."
"A mortal beast I would not expect to forage the same place every time."
"However, spirit beasts can have unusual behavior, though they are far more rare."
"So you have two options: the likely behavior from an unlikely source."
"Or the unlikely behavior from a likely source."
"I cannot tell you which it is in this case, but it would be wise to be ready for both."
Tie Bo hears her out without a flicker, then shakes his head slowly.
"A boar comes back to a place it likes. Again and again, till it's cleaned out or killed."

memory.fact: Tie Bo knows a boar will come back again and again to a feeding place it likes; he finds it natural.
Tie Bo knows a boar will come back again and again to a feeding place it likes; he finds it natural.

event: "That part's natural. Zhao Jun's rice is just the first it meets, coming down the river."

memory.fact: He thinks it hits Zhao Jun's terraces because they are the first rice it meets coming downriver.
He thinks it hits Zhao Jun's terraces because they are the first rice it meets coming downriver.

event: "It's the size that isn't natural."
"I tracked it twice this spring. Up to a wallow in a boggy hollow, below the gorge."

memory.fact: He tracked the great boar twice this spring, to a wallow in a boggy hollow below the gorge.
He tracked the great boar twice this spring, to a wallow in a boggy hollow below the gorge.
The boar's wallow lies in a boggy hollow below the gorge, ringed by torn-up earth.

event: "By the prints and the wallow, it's as heavy as two buffalo. No boar is that big."

memory.fact: From its prints and wallow he judges the boar as heavy as two buffalo, which no boar should be.
From its prints and wallow he judges the boar as heavy as two buffalo, which no boar should be.

event: He lifts a hand well above his own head. "Tusk marks on the pines. Up here."

memory.fact: He has found its tusk-scars on pines higher than his own head.
He has found its tusk-scars on pines higher than his own head.

event: He is quiet a moment, looking at the shrine lamp.
"Last autumn a boar gored my brother. Tie Shan. A torn-eared boar, big even then."

memory.fact: Last autumn a torn-eared boar gored his brother Tie Shan, who died of the wound before winter.
Last autumn a torn-eared boar gored his brother Tie Shan, who died of the wound before winter.

event: "I put my spear in its flank before it broke away. Shan died of the wound before winter."

memory.fact: Tie Bo put his spear into that boar's flank before it broke away into the woods.
Tie Bo put his spear into that boar's flank before it broke away into the woods.

event: "My grandfather told of a white stag in the hills, long ago. A spirit beast. I never saw one."

memory.fact: He has never seen a spirit beast; his grandfather told of a white stag in the hills long ago.
He has never seen a spirit beast; his grandfather told of a white stag in the hills long ago.

event: "I think it's the same boar. I think it's grown into something no spear was made for."

memory.fact: He fears the great boar is his brother's killer grown into something no spear was made for.
He fears the great boar is his brother's killer grown into something no spear was made for.

event: He says it flatly, but his jaw is tight.
"Here is how I'd do it. From dusk tomorrow, we watch the broken wall. Downwind."

memory.fact: He would watch the broken wall from dusk, downwind, with a line of sharpened stakes before it.
He would watch the broken wall from dusk, downwind, with a line of sharpened stakes before it.

event: "A line of sharpened stakes in front of it. Me behind them with the barred spear."
"Two steady men beside me. The Fang boys uphill with torches and gongs, to drive it down on us."

memory.fact: He would put himself with the iron-barred spear behind the stakes, and two steady men beside him.
He would put himself with the iron-barred spear behind the stakes, and two steady men beside him.
He would set the Fangs with torches and gongs uphill, to drive the boar down onto the stakes.
He would set the Fangs with torches and gongs uphill, to drive the boar down onto the stakes.

event: He looks at her again, straight on.
"I'd want you there, honored spirit. Out of the line. Behind us, safe."
"If you can tell what it is by the look of it, I need to know before I set my spear."

memory.fact: He would want the spirit there, out of the line, in hope she can tell what the beast is by sight.
He would want the spirit there, out of the line, in hope she can tell what the beast is by sight.

event: "Will you come?"
